51. Most Data Problems Are Not Big Data Problems大多数数据问题不是大数据问题

Thomas Nield

托马斯·尼尔德

When the big data buzzword peaked in 2015, I remember NoSQL, Hadoop, MongoDB, and other unstructured data technologies being touted as the future of analytics. Many organizations started collecting data faster than they could organize and store it, so they simply dumped it on a cluster and scaled horizontally as needed. Many companies put enormous expense into migrating off relational databases like MySQL and onto big data platforms like Apache Hadoop.

当大数据这个热词在 2015 年达到顶峰时，我记得 NoSQL、Hadoop、MongoDB 和其他非结构化数据技术被吹捧为分析的未来。许多组织开始收集数据的速度超过了他们整理和存储数据的速度，于是干脆把数据倒在一个集群上，按需横向扩展。许多公司花巨资从 MySQL 这样的关系数据库迁到 Apache Hadoop 这样的大数据平台。

Amidst this movement, I was teaching an O'Reilly online training on SQL. I had one participant suggest that relational databases and SQL might be legacy technology. If the lack of horizontal scaling was not enough reason, relational databases have all this pesky overhead to structure data in a normalized fashion, as well as to enforce data validation and primary/foreign keys. The internet and connectivity of devices caused an explosion of data, so scalability became the selling point of NoSQL and big data.

在这股潮流中，我正在教一门 O'Reilly 的 SQL 在线课。有位学员提出关系数据库和 SQL 可能是遗留技术。如果说缺乏横向扩展还不算充分理由，关系数据库还有一堆烦人的开销——要把数据规范化地结构化、要做数据校验、要强制主键/外键。互联网和设备联网导致数据爆炸，于是可扩展性成了 NoSQL 和大数据的卖点。

The irony is that SQL interfaces were added to these big data platforms, and this happened for a reason. Analysts found NoSQL languages difficult and wanted to analyze data in a relational data fashion. A great majority of data problems are best modeled as relational database structures. An ORDER has a CUSTOMER and a PRODUCT associated with it. It just makes sense that these pieces of information should be normalized in separate tables rather than as a blob of JSON. Even better, there's peace of mind knowing the database software will validate an ORDER and check that the CUSTOMER and PRODUCT do, in fact, exist, rather than let data corruption quietly creep in because of bugs on the frontend.

讽刺的是，这些大数据平台后来都加上了 SQL 接口，这不是没有原因的。分析师发现 NoSQL 语言很难用，想用关系数据的方式分析数据。绝大多数数据问题最好用关系数据库结构来建模。一个订单（ORDER）关联着一个客户（CUSTOMER）和一个商品（PRODUCT）。这些信息被规范化到不同的表里、而不是塞成一坨 JSON，才是合理的。更妙的是，你可以安心地知道数据库软件会校验订单、检查客户和商品是否真的存在，而不是因为前端 bug 让数据腐烂悄悄渗透进来。

The truth is, most data problems are not big data problems. Anecdotally, 99.9% of problems I've encountered are best solved with a traditional relational database.

真相是，大多数数据问题不是大数据问题。凭经验说，我遇到的 99.9% 的问题，用传统关系数据库解决最好。

— p.123 —

Valid cases for using NoSQL platforms definitely exist, especially when an enormous amount of unstructured data has to be stored (think social media posts, news articles, and web scrapes). But with operational data, relational databases force you to think carefully about how your data model works and to get it right the first time. Operational data of this nature rarely gets so large that a relational database cannot be scaled.

使用 NoSQL 平台的正当案例当然存在，尤其是在要存储海量非结构化数据时（想想社交媒体帖子、新闻文章、网页抓取）。但对运营数据，关系数据库会迫使你仔细思考数据模型如何运作，并在第一次就把它做对。这种性质的运营数据很少会大到关系数据库扩展不了的程度。

I will leave you with the following table to help aid your SQL-versus-NoSQL decisions.

我留给你下面这张表，帮你做 SQL 与 NoSQL 的决策。

FeatureSQLNoSQLWinner
Integrity/consistency
完整性/一致性		Data is enforced with logical relationships, minimized redundancy, and "up-to-date" consistency.
通过逻辑关系强制数据完整性、最小化冗余、并保证“最新”一致性。		Simple key/value and document storage does not enforce any rules or structure. Redundancy and write latency are common.
简单的键值和文档存储不强制任何规则或结构。冗余和写延迟很常见。		SQL
Design changes
设计变更		Easy to "add" to a database, but harder to modify one.
向数据库“加”东西容易，但修改已有的难。		NoSQL can quickly and arbitrarily change what data it stores.
NoSQL 可以快速、任意地改变它存储的数据。		NoSQL

SQL 是通用语言，让访问和分析数据变得简单。		SQL support is sparse, and proprietary languages are esoteric and hardly universal.
SQL 支持稀疏，专有语言晦涩且几乎不通用。		SQL

Java、Python、.NET 程序员要把实体映射到表，可能很繁琐。但数据完整性是给定的。		Programming against a NoSQL database is quick and simple, but the onus is on the programmer to validate data.

NoSQL 能通过横向扩展存储海量数据。由于横向扩展和没有完整性约束，它也跑得快。		NoSQL

52. Moving from Software Engineering to Data Engineering从软件工程转向数据工程

John Salinas

约翰·萨利纳斯

The move from software engineering to data engineering is rewarding and exciting. Data engineering is everything software engineering is: passion and principles for solving technical challenges efficiently and elegantly. But you expand your craft to include analytical and data-related problems. This involves solving problems at an even larger scale, and also helping people find insights from the problems you are solving.

从软件工程转到数据工程是有回报且令人兴奋的。数据工程具备软件工程的一切：以高效优雅的方式解决技术挑战的热情和原则。但你把手艺扩展到了分析和数据相关的问题。这涉及解决更大规模的问题，也帮助人们从你正在解决的问题中找到洞见。

When I first started in data engineering, I felt lost because there was so much to learn. But like you, I love learning. I was thrilled by the challenge to learn new technologies and new patterns. It's been comforting to realize that all the same principles still apply—things like using abstraction, keeping things simple, and building applications so they are scalable and easy to maintain. Also, all my experience is still relevant, and even more important, so are skills like troubleshooting, scaling enterprise applications, API development, networking, programming, and scripting.

我刚开始做数据工程时，觉得很迷失，因为要学的东西太多了。但和你一样，我热爱学习。学习新技术、新模式的挑战让我兴奋。让人欣慰的是，我意识到所有同样的原则依然适用——比如用抽象、保持简单、把应用建得可扩展易维护。而且我所有的经验仍然有用，更重要的是，像排障、企业应用扩展、API 开发、网络、编程、脚本这些技能也都有用。

With data engineering, you solve problems similar to those in software engineering, but at a larger scale. I've worked on code that processes billions of events. I wore it as a badge of honor that traditional technologies and platforms would break with the amount of information we were trying to process. Early on, we broke our relational database; when we tried to replicate the data to another database, the replication process could not keep up. Also, one time in our Hadoop environment, we lost over 170TB of data. Don't worry; we were able to recover it, but I was shocked at how much data our project was processing.

在数据工程里，你解决和软件工程类似的问题，但规模更大。我做过处理数十亿事件的代码。传统技术和平台在我们要处理的信息量下会崩，我把这当作荣誉徽章。早期我们搞崩了关系数据库；当我们试图把数据复制到另一个数据库时，复制进程跟不上。还有一次在 Hadoop 环境里，我们丢了超过 170TB 数据。别担心，我们恢复了，但我震惊于我们项目处理的数据量之大。

And it's not just technology that you break; you also end up breaking mindsets. As a developer, you are comfortable with arrays, structs, objects, enums, and JSON format, but when you introduce these concepts to analysts familiar with only tabular data and primitive data types, it creates an opportunity to teach them about these new things.

而且你搞崩的不只是技术；你还会搞崩思维定势。作为开发者，你对数组、结构体、对象、枚举、JSON 格式习以为常，但当你把这些概念介绍给只熟悉表格数据和原始数据类型的分析师时，就创造了教他们这些新东西的机会。

— p.125 —

With all of these challenges, you have to rethink traditional approaches and get creative when solving problems. Your day-to-day challenges grow from operational use cases to including analytical use cases too. The infrastructure you create not only has to support real-time production traffic that could be customer-facing but also provide insights to analysts looking for patterns in the massive amounts of data in your application. It's an engineering challenge to support both at the same time.

面对所有这些挑战，你必须重新思考传统方法，在解决问题时发挥创造力。你日常的挑战从运营用例扩展到了分析用例。你创建的基础设施不仅要支持面向客户的实时生产流量，还要为在应用海量数据中寻找模式的分析师提供洞见。同时支持两者是一项工程挑战。

Moving to data engineering provides many exciting benefits. It allows you to learn new things. It allows you to mentor folks based on your experience. And it allows you to solve unique and large problems.

转到数据工程带来许多令人兴奋的好处。它让你学到新东西。它让你基于自己的经验指导他人。它让你解决独特而宏大的问题。

— p.126 —

53. Observability for Data Engineers数据工程师的可观测性

Barr Moses

巴尔·摩西

As companies become increasingly data driven, the technologies underlying the rich insights data provides have grown more nuanced and complex. Our ability to collect, store, aggregate, and visualize this data has largely kept up with the needs of modern data teams (think domain-oriented data meshes, cloud warehouses, and data-modeling solutions), but the mechanics behind data quality and integrity have lagged.

随着公司日益数据驱动，数据所提供的丰富洞见背后的技术变得更加精细和复杂。我们收集、存储、聚合和可视化这些数据的能力，基本跟上了现代数据团队的需求（想想面向领域的数据网格、云数仓、数据建模方案），但数据质量和完整性背后的机制却落后了。

How Good Data Turns Bad好数据是怎么变坏的

After speaking with several hundred data-engineering teams, I've noticed three primary reasons for good data turning bad:

在和几百个数据工程团队聊过之后，我注意到好数据变坏主要有三个原因：

  • More and more data sources. Nowadays, companies use anywhere from dozens to hundreds of internal and external data sources to produce analytics and ML models. Any one of these sources can change in unexpected ways and without notice, compromising the data the company uses to make decisions.
    越来越多的数据源。如今，公司使用几十到几百个内部和外部数据源来产出分析和 ML 模型。其中任何一个源都可能以意外的方式、在没有通知的情况下变化，损害公司用来做决策的数据。
  • Increasingly complex data pipelines. Data pipelines are increasingly complex, with multiple stages of processing and nontrivial dependencies among various data assets. With little visibility into these dependencies, any change made to one dataset can impact the correctness of dependent data assets.
    日益复杂的数据管道。数据管道越来越复杂，有多个处理阶段和各种数据资产之间不简单的依赖。由于对这些依赖几乎不可见，对一个数据集的任何变更都可能影响下游数据资产的正确性。
  • Bigger, more specialized data teams. Companies are increasingly hiring more and more data analysts, scientists, and engineers to build and maintain the data pipelines, analytics, and ML models that power their services and products. Miscommunication is inevitable and will cause these complex systems to break as changes are made.
    更大、更专业的数据团队。公司越来越多地雇佣数据分析师、科学家、工程师来构建和维护支撑服务与产品的数据管道、分析和 ML 模型。沟通失误不可避免，并会在变更时让这些复杂系统出故障。
— p.127 —

Introducing Data Observability认识数据可观测性

The good news? Data engineering is going through its own renaissance, and we owe a big thank you to our counterparts in DevOps.

好消息呢？数据工程正在经历自己的复兴，这要大大感谢 DevOps 的同行们。

For the past decade or so, software engineers have leveraged targeted solutions to ensure high application uptime while keeping downtime to a minimum. In data, we call this phenomenon data downtime. This refers to periods of time when data is partial, erroneous, missing, or otherwise inaccurate, and it only multiplies as data systems become increasingly complex. By applying the same principles of software application observability and reliability to data, these issues can be identified, resolved, and even prevented, giving data teams confidence in their data so they can deliver valuable insights. Data observability has five pillars.¹

过去十年左右，软件工程师利用有针对性的解决方案，确保应用高可用、最小化停机。在数据领域，我们把这个现象称为数据停机。它指的是数据不完整、错误、缺失、或以其他方式不准确的时间段；随着数据系统日益复杂，它只会成倍放大。通过把软件应用可观测性和可靠性的同样原则应用到数据上，这些问题可以被识别、解决甚至预防，让数据团队对数据有信心，从而交付有价值的洞见。数据可观测性有五大支柱。¹

Each pillar encapsulates a series of questions that, in aggregate, provide a holistic view of data health:

每个支柱都封装了一系列问题，这些问题合在一起提供数据健康的整体视图：

  • Freshness. Is the data recent? When was the last time it was generated? What upstream data is included/omitted?
    新鲜度。数据是新的吗？上次生成是什么时候？包含/遗漏了哪些上游数据？
  • Distribution. Is the data within accepted ranges? Is it properly formatted? Is it complete?
    分布。数据在可接受范围内吗？格式正确吗？完整吗？
  • Volume. Has all the data arrived?
    数据量。所有数据都到了吗？
  • Schema. How has the schema changed? Who has made these changes, and for what reasons?
    Schema。schema 怎么变了？谁做了这些变更？出于什么原因？
  • Lineage. What are the upstream and downstream assets impacted by a given data asset? Who are the people generating this data, and who is relying on it for decision making?
    血缘。一个给定数据资产会影响哪些上下游资产？谁在产生这份数据？谁在依赖它做决策？

As data leaders increasingly invest in data-reliability solutions that leverage data observability, I anticipate that this field will continue to intersect with other major trends in data engineering, including data meshes, machine learning, cloud data architectures, and the delivery of data products as platforms.

随着数据负责人越来越多地投资于利用数据可观测性的数据可靠性方案，我预计这个领域将继续与数据工程的其他主要趋势相交，包括数据网格、机器学习、云数据架构、以及把数据产品作为平台交付。

¹ Image courtesy of Monte Carlo.

¹ 图片由 Monte Carlo 提供。

— p.128 —

54. Perfect Is the Enemy of Good完美是好的敌人

Bob Haffner

鲍勃·哈夫纳

"Le mieux est l'ennemi du bien," loosely translated as "Perfect is the enemy of good," is a saying that most attribute to Voltaire. It's a cautionary phrase about the perceived value of chasing perfection versus the reality of it. This phrase can apply to numerous domains, including data engineering.

"Le mieux est l'ennemi du bien"——大意是“完美是好的敌人”——是一句常被归于伏尔泰的谚语。它警示人们追逐完美的感知价值与现实之间的差距。这句话可以应用于许多领域，包括数据工程。

Suggesting that perfection is not the goal often invites skepticism from data engineers. After all, developing data products requires precision and a detail-oriented approach. Further, most data engineers have been a part of rushed implementations only to have it come back to haunt them. Sprinkle in a natural aversion to risk, and there are multiple reasons people would challenge the notion that stopping short of perfection is a good idea.

提出“完美不是目标”常常引来数据工程师的怀疑。毕竟，开发数据产品需要精确和注重细节的方法。而且，大多数数据工程师都经历过赶工实现、结果回来找自己算账的情况。再加上对风险的自然厌恶，人们有很多理由质疑“适可而止、不求完美”是个好主意。

However, this is not a plea for shortcuts. Instead, I'm advocating for delivering faster and implementing only the valuable features.

然而，这不是在呼吁走捷径。相反，我主张的是更快地交付、只实现有价值的功能。

This concept of delivering faster is similar to Agile's principle of shipping a minimum viable product (MVP). The value of quickly putting a product in the hands of a user cannot be overstated. For example, if your leaders require three metrics to run the business and you have only one completed, ship it. Driving the organization with some insight is always better than driving with none.

更快交付的理念与敏捷的最小可行产品（MVP）原则相似。把产品快速交到用户手中的价值怎么强调都不为过。例如，如果你的领导需要三个指标来运营业务，而你只完成了一个，就先发出去。带着一些洞见驱动组织，总比毫无洞见地驱动要好。

The only thing that might be worse than waiting to ship a viable product is developing the remaining features in the pursuit of perfection. These remaining features can often take longer to implement than others or provide less value, or both. For example, if adding a dashboard visualization for a single user requires breaking model and pipeline changes, the payoff probably does not warrant the effort. All of a solution's proposed features should be scrutinized for their projected return on investment, but be particularly vigilant about ones at the bottom of the priority list.

唯一可能比“等着发一个可行产品”更糟的事，是为了追求完美去开发剩余功能。这些剩余功能往往实现起来更慢、或价值更低，或者两者皆是。例如，如果为单个用户加一个仪表盘可视化需要破坏模型和管道变更，回报可能不值得这份努力。一个方案提出的所有功能都应被审视其预期投资回报，但对优先级列表底部的功能要格外警惕。

— p.130 —

Data engineering is a challenging endeavor that is often fraught with complexity. By delivering faster and implementing only the valuable features, you can reduce the risk and increase your chances of success.

数据工程是一项充满挑战的工作，常常伴随着复杂度。通过更快交付、只实现有价值的功能，你可以降低风险、提高成功几率。

— p.131 —

55. Pipe Dreams管道之梦

Scott Haines (Senior principal software engineer/software architect)

斯科特·海恩斯（资深首席软件工程师/软件架构师）

One subtle and novel paradigm in computer systems architecture is the concept of message passing. This simple, albeit useful construct allowed for an order of magnitude of gains in parallel processing by allowing processes (applications, kernel tasks, etc.) within a single computer OS to take part in a conversation. The beauty of this was that processes could now participate in conversations in either synchronous or asynchronous fashion and distribute work among many applications without the necessary overhead of locking and synchronization.

计算机系统架构中一个微妙而新颖的范式是消息传递。这个简单却有用的构造，通过让单机操作系统内的进程（应用、内核任务等）参与对话，让并行处理获得了数量级的提升。它的美妙之处在于：进程现在可以同步或异步地参与对话，并在多个应用之间分配工作，而不需要加锁和同步的必要开销。

This novel approach to solving parallel processing tasks within a single system was further expanded to distributed systems processing with the advent of the message queue as a service. The basic message queue allowed for one or many channels (or topics) to be created in a distributed first-in, first-out (FIFO) style of queue that could be run as a service on top of a network-addressable location (e.g., ip-address:port). Now many systems across many servers could communicate in a distributed, shared work style, a decomposition of tasks.

这种在单系统内解决并行处理任务的新方法，随着消息队列即服务的出现，进一步扩展到分布式系统处理。基础消息队列允许在一个分布式先进先出（FIFO）队列中创建一个或多个通道（或主题），这个队列可以作为服务运行在一个网络可达位置（例如 ip-address:port）之上。现在，跨多台服务器的许多系统可以以分布式、共享工作的方式通信，这是任务的一种分解。

It isn't hard to conceptualize how the pipeline architecture grew out of the concept of distributed systems communicating over network-addressable message queues. It kind of makes sense on a macro level. Essentially, we had all of the components of the modern pipeline architecture sitting on the assembly line, just waiting to be assembled. But first we had to solve a tiny little issue: failure in the face of partially processed messages.

不难想象管道架构是如何从“分布式系统通过网络可达的消息队列通信”这个概念中长出来的。宏观上讲得通。本质上，现代管道架构的所有组件都已经摆在装配线上，只等组装。但我们得先解决一个小问题：在面对部分处理过的消息时的失败。

As you may imagine, if we have a distributed queue and take a message from that queue, we can assume that the queue will purge said message, and life will go on. However, in the face of failure—no matter where you point the blame—if the message is purged before the work is done, that will result in data loss with no means of recovery. Now this is where things evolved. Given that we wanted to ensure that our applications would complete all work they took from the queue, it made sense to store a log of the messages within a channel (or topic), and allow our systems to keep track of what they consumed and essentially where their processing left off.

你可以想象，如果我们有一个分布式队列，从中取一条消息，可以假设队列会清掉这条消息，生活继续。然而面对失败——无论你把责任推给谁——如果消息在工作完成前就被清掉，就会导致数据丢失、无法恢复。事情就是在这里演进的。鉴于我们想确保应用完成从队列取出的所有工作，在通道（或主题）内存储消息日志、让系统跟踪自己消费了什么、处理到哪儿停了下来，就成了合理选择。

— p.132 —

This simple idea of acknowledging where an application was in the queue led to the concept of offset tracking and checkpointing for a consumer group within a queue. Apache Kafka was the first project that treated a message queue as a reliable and, more importantly, replay-able queue that could easily be divided and shared among multiple applications within a shared consumer group. Now there was a reliable, highly available, and highly scalable system that could be used for more than just message passing, and this essentially created the foundation of the streaming pipeline architecture.

这种“确认应用在队列中处理到哪儿”的简单想法，催生了队列中消费者组的偏移量跟踪和检查点概念。Apache Kafka 是第一个把消息队列当作可靠、更重要的是可重放队列的项目，可以在共享消费者组内的多个应用之间轻易分割和共享。现在有了一个可靠、高可用、高可扩展的系统，它的用途远超消息传递，这 essentially 奠定了流式管道架构的基础。

— p.133 —

56. Preventing the Data Lake Abyss防止数据湖深渊

Scott Haines (Senior principal software engineer/software architect)

斯科特·海恩斯（资深首席软件工程师/软件架构师）

Everyone has worked under the wrong assumptions at one point or another in their careers, and in no place have I found this more apparent than when it comes to legacy data and a lot of what ends up in most companies' data lakes.

每个人职业生涯中都有过在错误假设下工作的时候；而我发现，在遗留数据、以及最终进入大多数公司数据湖的那些东西上，这一点尤为明显。

The concept of the data lake evolved from the more traditional data warehouse, which was originally envisioned as a means to alleviate the issue of data silos and fragmentation within an organization. The data warehouse achieved this by providing a central store where all data can be accessed, usually through a traditional SQL interface or other business intelligence tools. The data lake takes this concept one step further and allows you to dump all of your data in its raw format (unstructured or structured) into a horizontally scalable massive data store (HDFS/S3) where it can be stored almost indefinitely.

数据湖的概念从更传统的数据仓库演进而来；数据仓库最初被设想为缓解组织内数据孤岛和数据碎片化问题的手段。数据仓库通过提供一个中央存储来实现这一点，所有数据都可在其中访问，通常通过传统 SQL 接口或其他商业智能工具。数据湖把这个概念又推进了一步：让你把所有数据以原始格式（非结构化或结构化）倒到一个水平扩展的海量存储（HDFS/S3）中，几乎可以无限期存放。

Over the course of many years, what usually starts with the best of intentions can easily turn into a black hole for your company's most valuable asset as underlying data formats change and render older data unusable. This problem seems to arise from three central issues:

多年过去，那些初衷良好的东西，随着底层数据格式变化、旧数据变得不可用，很容易变成吞噬公司最有价值资产的黑洞。这个问题似乎源于三个核心问题：

  • A basic lack of ownership for the team producing a given dataset
    对生产某个数据集的团队，缺乏基本的责任归属
  • A general lack of good etiquette or data hygiene when it comes to preserving backward compatibility with respect to legacy data structures
    在遗留数据结构的向后兼容方面，普遍缺乏良好的礼仪或数据卫生
  • Starting off on the wrong foot when creating a new dataset, with no support from other data-modeling or data-engineering experts
    创建新数据集时一开始就走错，没有其他数据建模或数据工程专家的支持

I have found that a simple approach to solving these data-consistency issues come from establishing what I call data contracts.

我发现，解决这些数据一致性问题的一个简单方法，是建立我所谓的数据契约。

— p.134 —

Establishing Data Contracts建立数据契约

The ever-growing need for quality data within an organization almost demands the establishment of data contracts ahead of time. This means taking things further than just adhering to and providing a schema for your data, to also generating a plan for or story about what fields exist when, where, and why.

组织内对高质量数据的需求不断增长，几乎要求提前建立数据契约。这意味着不只是遵守和提供数据 schema，还要进一步制定计划或故事，说明哪些字段在什么时候、在什么地方、为什么存在。

This contract is your data's API and should be updated and versioned with any change in your producing code. Knowing when a field will exist (or not) saves people time and reduces frustration.

这个契约就是你数据的 API，应随生产代码的任何变更而更新并版本化。知道一个字段什么时候存在（或不存在）能节省人们的时间、减少挫败。

From Generic Data Lake to Data Structure Store从通用数据湖到数据结构存储

Taking this idea to the next level requires the producing team to have compiled libraries for both producing and consuming their data. These libraries should also provide unit tests to ensure full backward compatibility across changes to the underlying data structures. Two commonly used data structure frameworks are Apache Avro and Google Protocol Buffers. Both allow you to define your data schemas in a platform-agnostic way and ultimately give you the type safety you'll never have with traditional JSON.

把这个想法提升到下一个层次，要求生产团队拥有用于生产和消费其数据的编译库。这些库还应提供单元测试，确保底层数据结构变更时完全向后兼容。两个常用的数据结构框架是 Apache Avro 和 Google Protocol Buffers。两者都允许你以平台无关的方式定义数据 schema，最终给你传统 JSON 永远给不了的类型安全。

These versioned and compiled libraries help ensure that each byte of data stored adheres to strict validation and is accountable to the version of the data contract. This establishes a simple rule that each record will be preserved in a versioned format that will be at the very least backward compatible and in a format that can easily be extracted and used for years to come. This up-front effort will lead to productivity across all data-consuming entities in your company. Instead of road maps being derailed with long periods of let's play find the missing data (or literally jettisoning or draining the lake to start over because of a general lack of trust in the data's integrity), you can get back to having a data lake that is an invaluable shared resource used for any of your data needs: from analytics to data science and on into the deep learning horizons.

这些版本化的编译库有助于确保存储的每字节数据都经过严格校验，并对数据契约的版本负责。这建立了一条简单规则：每条记录将以版本化格式保存，至少向后兼容，并以一种未来多年都能轻松提取和使用的格式保存。这种前期投入将在公司所有数据消费实体中带来生产力。你的路线图不会因为长时间“我们来找失踪数据吧”而脱轨（或者因为普遍不信任数据完整性而干脆把湖抽干重来），你可以重新拥有一个数据湖——一个用于满足任何数据需求的无价共享资源：从分析到数据科学，再到深度学习的远方。

— p.135 —

57. Prioritizing User Experience in Messaging Systems在消息系统中优先考虑用户体验

Jowanza Joseph

乔万扎·约瑟夫

Resource efficiency is one reason to utilize a messaging system, but the user experience may ultimately be a more compelling one. The software systems we use and rely on to manage our finances, run our businesses, and ensure our health all benefit from user experience enhancements. These enhancements can come in several forms, but the most notable are improving the design to make interfaces more comfortable to navigate and doing more on behalf of the user. Programs that perform on the user's behalf quickly and accurately can take an everyday experience and turn it into something magical. Consider a bank account that saves money on your behalf by using your balance and other context to deposit money in your savings account. Over time you save money without ever feeling the pain of saving. Messaging systems are the backbone of systems like this one and enable rich user experiences.

资源效率是使用消息系统的一个理由，但用户体验最终可能是一个更有说服力的理由。我们用来管理财务、经营业务、保障健康的软件系统，都从用户体验增强中受益。这些增强可以有多种形式，但最显著的是改善设计让界面导航更舒适、以及替用户做更多事。替用户快速准确执行的程序，可以把日常体验变成某种神奇的东西。想想一个银行账户：它替你存钱，利用你的余额和其他上下文，把钱存进你的储蓄账户。久而久之，你没感到存钱的痛苦就攒下了钱。消息系统就是这类系统的骨干，让丰富的用户体验成为可能。

Consider another example from banking. In many cases, borrowing money requires printing out your bank statements, pay stubs, tax statements, and more so the bank can get an understanding of your monthly expenses. Frequently, these documents are required to prequalify for a loan and are required again two months later to get the actual loan. While this sounds painful and superfluous in an era of technology, the bank has good reason to be as thorough and intrusive as possible to manage risk and comply with regulations.

再举一个银行业的例子。很多情况下，借钱需要你打印银行对账单、工资单、税单等等，好让银行了解你的月支出。这些文件常常在预审贷款时需要，两个月后真正放款时还要再交一次。虽然在科技时代这听起来既痛苦又多余，但银行有充分理由尽可能彻底和侵入，以管理风险和遵守法规。

To modernize this credit approval system, we need to think about the problem through a slightly different lens. Here's one approach: after a customer prequalifies, the software system connected to the user's financial institution will send notifications to the lending company for predetermined events. The lender is notified in real time if the potential borrower does anything that would jeopardize the loan closing. In real time, the lender can update based on the borrower's behavior how much they can borrow and have a clear understanding of the probability that the loan will close successfully. After the initial data collection from prequalification, a real-time pipeline of transactions and credit usage is sent to the lender, so there are no surprises.

要让这个信贷审批系统现代化，我们需要用略为不同的视角来看问题。下面是一种方法：客户预审通过后，连接用户金融机构的软件系统会就预定事件向贷款公司发送通知。如果潜在借款人做了任何危及贷款放款的事，贷款方会收到实时通知。贷款方可以基于借款人行为实时更新可借额度，并清楚了解贷款成功放款的概率。预审初始数据收集之后，交易和信用使用的实时管道会发给贷款方，因此不会有意外。

— p.136 —

When something goes wrong in the medical field, it can be much more devastating than losing money. Mistakes in the medical field can lead to permanent injury and death for a patient, disbarment for a medical provider, or a lawsuit for a hospital system.

在医疗领域出问题，比损失金钱要毁灭性得多。医疗领域的错误可能导致病人永久伤害甚至死亡、医疗从业者被吊销执照，或医院系统被起诉。

Of all patient complaints, the most common was that patients felt frustrated by having to give their medical history more than once per visit. How might a real-time system help the hospital?

在所有病人投诉中，最常见的是病人感到沮丧——每次就诊都要把病史重复说一遍。实时系统如何能帮医院？

The software engineering department and health providers at a Utah hospital worked together to reimagine what the health history system could look like. When a patient arrived at the hospital, they would enter their information on a tablet. Once complete, the data would be saved to the system. Three minutes before the scheduled appointment time, the doctor would receive a notification to log on and check the patient's information. During that time, they would end their previous appointment and start reading through the new patient's chart. When the doctor arrived in the patient's room, they would know everything they needed to know to start a conversation with the patient about their care.

犹他州一家医院的软件工程部门和医疗人员一起，重新构想病史系统可以是什么样子。病人到达医院时，在平板上录入信息。完成后，数据存入系统。预约时间前三分钟，医生会收到通知登录查看病人信息。在这三分钟里，他们结束上一个预约，开始阅读新病人的病历。当医生走进病房时，他们已经知道开始和病人谈论其护理所需知道的一切。

This system even provided benefits after the initial consultation, including enabling the doctor to send test orders directly to the lab and auto-populating patient data when the patient checked in at the lab.

这个系统甚至在初诊之后也带来好处，包括让医生直接把检查单发给实验室，并在病人到实验室签到时自动填入病人数据。

While initially designed to prevent duplicate collection of medical histories, the system ended up having a far-reaching impact on the hospital system. Not only did the hospital system save money, but the patient experience improved dramatically.

虽然最初设计目的是防止重复采集病史，这个系统最终对医院系统产生了深远影响。医院系统不仅省了钱，病人体验也大幅改善。

— p.137 —

58. Privacy Is Your Problem隐私是你的问题

Stephen Bailey, PhD

斯蒂芬·贝利 博士

Data has been called "the new gold" for its ability to transform and automate business processes; it has also been called "the new uranium" for its ability to violate the human right to privacy on a massive scale. And just as nuclear engineers can effortlessly enumerate fundamental differences in gold and uranium, so too must data engineers learn to instinctively identify and separate dangerous data from the benign.

数据因其能变革和自动化业务流程而被称为“新黄金”；它也因其能大规模侵犯人类隐私权而被称为“新铀”。正如核工程师能毫不费力地列举黄金和铀的根本区别，数据工程师也必须学会本能地识别并把危险数据从良性数据中分离出来。

Take, for instance, the famous link attack that reidentified the medical records of several high-profile patients of Massachusetts General Hospital. In 1997, MGH released about 15,000 records in which names and patient IDs had been stripped from the database. Despite the precautions, Harvard researcher Latanya Sweeney was able to connect publicly available voter information to these anonymized medical records by joining them on three indirect identifiers: zip code, birthdate, and gender. This left Sweeney with only a handful of records to sift through to reidentify many individuals—most notably, the governor of Massachusetts patient records.

举个例子，著名的链接攻击重新识别了麻省总医院几位知名患者的医疗记录。1997 年，MGH 发布了大约 15000 条记录，其中姓名和病人 ID 已从数据库中剥离。尽管有这些预防措施，哈佛研究员 Latanya Sweeney 仍能通过三个间接标识符——邮编、出生日期、性别——把公开可用的选民信息与这些匿名医疗记录连接起来。这让 Sweeney 只需筛极少记录就能重新识别出许多人——最著名的是马萨诸塞州州长的病历。

Twenty years later, every business is an MGH, and every person with internet access is a potential Latanya Sweeney. Yet we all want a world where data is handled responsibly, shared cautiously, and leveraged only for the right purposes. Our greatest limitation in realizing that world is not one of possibility but responsibility; it's not a question of "How?" but "Who?"

二十年后，每个企业都是一个 MGH，每个有网络的人都是潜在的 Latanya Sweeney。然而我们都想要一个数据被负责任地处理、谨慎共享、只用于正当目的的世界。实现这个世界最大的局限不是可能性，而是责任；问题不是“怎么做”，而是“谁来做”。

I believe data engineers must be the ones to take ownership of the problem and lead. Controlling the reidentifiability of records through a single dashboard is good analytics hygiene, but preserving privacy in the platform delivering the data is crucial. Managing privacy loss is a systemic problem demanding systemic solutions—and data engineers build the systems.

我相信数据工程师必须是担起这个问题并牵头的人。通过一个单一仪表盘控制记录的可重识别性，是良好的分析卫生，但在交付数据的平台中保护隐私至关重要。管理隐私损失是一个系统性问题，需要系统性解决方案——而系统正是数据工程师建的。

The mandate to protect privacy does not translate to a boring exercise in implementing business logic; it presents exciting new technical challenges. How can we quantify the degree of privacy protection we are providing? How can we rebuild data products—and guarantee they still function—after an individual requests that their data be deleted? How can we translate sprawling legal regulations into comprehensible data policies while satisfying data-hungry consumers?

保护隐私的要求并不等于在业务逻辑实现中做枯燥练习；它呈现了令人兴奋的新技术挑战。我们如何量化我们提供的隐私保护程度？在个人请求删除其数据后，我们如何重建数据产品——并保证它们仍然正常工作？我们如何把庞杂的法律法规翻译成可理解的数据策略，同时满足饥渴的数据消费方？

— p.138 —

We will need to formulate a new set of engineering best practices that extend beyond the familiar domains of security and system design. Determining what is best practice requires much practice, though. It is essential that engineering leaders push their teams to understand and address the pertinent issues: the strengths and weaknesses of data masking, anonymization techniques like k-anonymization and differential privacy, and emerging technologies such as federated learning. Ultimately, data engineers should know the practice of privacy by design as intuitively as they do the principle of least privilege.

我们需要制定一套新的工程最佳实践，超越熟悉的安全和系统设计领域。但要确定什么是最佳实践，需要大量实践。工程负责人必须推动团队理解和处理相关问题：数据掩码的优缺点、k-匿名和差分隐私等匿名化技术、以及联邦学习等新兴技术。最终，数据工程师应当像熟知最小权限原则一样，直觉般地熟知“隐私 by design”的实践。

The alternative, if history is any guide, is a world in which institutions publish "anonymized" data to the world, and clever people and organizations reconstruct and repurpose private data for their own ends. Managing privacy, far from being an abstract concept for just philosophers and lawyers, has become a concrete problem perfectly suited for data engineers. It's time they made it their own.

如果以历史为鉴，另一种结果是：机构向世界发布“匿名化”数据，而聪明的人和组织重构并把私人数据用于自己的目的。管理隐私远不只是哲学家和律师的抽象概念，它已经成为一个完全适合数据工程师的具体问题。是时候把它变成他们自己的问题了。

— p.139 —

59. QA and All Its SexinessQA 及其全部性感之处

Sonia Mehta

索尼娅·梅塔

Before moving into a new home, prospective homeowners will hire an inspector to assess any damage within the house. Much like house inspectors, as data engineers, it's on us to spot any glaring and not-so-glaring issues with our data before sending it to production.

搬进新家之前，准房主会请验房师评估房子里的损坏。和验房师很像，作为数据工程师，我们有责任在数据上线前发现那些显眼和不那么显眼的问题。

Setting up a quality assurance (QA) program is simple, and the gains are totally worth it! In setting up a QA program, tests can be divided into two major buckets: practical and logical.

建立一个质量保证（QA）流程很简单，收益完全值得！在建立 QA 流程时，测试可以分成两大类：实践性测试和逻辑性测试。

Practical tests aim to test for completeness of the data and accurate data types. These include the following:

实践性测试旨在测试数据完整性和数据类型正确性。包括：

  • Checking for data coverage by inspecting dates or expected row counts
    通过检查日期或预期行数来核对数据覆盖度
  • Standardizing currency inputs (e.g., removing commas from metrics)
    标准化货币输入（例如去掉指标里的逗号）
  • Ensuring that required fields contain no null values
    确保必填字段不含空值
  • Validating for consistent date, time zone, and casing formats
    校验日期、时区、大小写格式一致
  • Confirming that headers are applied to data and not within the data itself
    确认表头是作用在数据上、而不是混在数据本身里
  • Deduping the dataset
    对数据集去重

Logical tests are for business and domain relevance. This is the fun part! Integral to this step is obtaining a macro business context and understanding the main questions looking to be answered. It's also helpful to understand how important accuracy is to the stakeholder. Is directional accuracy sufficient, or is complete accuracy required? (Oftentimes finance teams will say that total accuracy is required, whereas other teams may be looking for only directional differences.)

逻辑性测试用于业务和领域相关性。这是有趣的部分！这一步的核心是获得宏观业务上下文、理解要回答的主要问题。理解准确性对利益相关者有多重要也很有帮助。方向上准确就够了，还是需要完全准确？（财务团队常常说需要完全准确，而其他团队可能只想要方向差异。）

This step includes applying subject-matter knowledge to the tests. For example:

这一步包括把领域知识应用到测试中。例如：

  • Every user in a trial should have $0 in their purchases total.
    试用期中的每个用户，其购买总额都应为 $0。
  • The attribution event counts only if it happened before the installation, not after.
    归因事件只有在安装之前发生才算数，之后发生不算。
  • The two sample sizes in the experiment should be within 1% of each other.
    实验中两组样本量应相差不超过 1%。
  • Free users will never have access to these parts of the app, and therefore no data.
    免费用户永远访问不到应用的这些部分，因此不应有数据。
  • If a user is refunded, ensure that the amount is deducted from the date of the refund, not the date of purchase.
    如果用户被退款，确保金额从退款日期起扣，而不是购买日期。
— p.140 —

Here are some additional notes on the QA process:

下面是关于 QA 流程的一些补充说明：

  • The test is an equation. Assert what you expect for the field and compare this to the actual value. Voilà!
    测试就是一个方程。断言你对字段的预期值，和实际值比较。瞧！
  • Tools can help automate these tests during the development process to ensure consistency, accuracy, and stability.
    工具可以在开发过程中自动化这些测试，以保证一致性、准确性和稳定性。
  • Use a linter!
    用 linter！
  • It's OK to have code rules. For example, maybe you want all True/False columns to begin with an is prefix, like is_.
    有代码规则是 OK 的。例如，你可能希望所有布尔列都以 is_ 开头，比如 is_<问题>。
  • As more people enter the organization and small changes across many individuals multiply, a well-thought-out QA program will help mitigate breakage.
    随着更多人加入组织、许多人的小变更相乘，一个深思熟虑的 QA 流程会帮助减少破坏。
  • If you have more than one source of truth for a metric, use this as a QA method to keep both metrics in check.
    如果一个指标有多个事实源，把这当作 QA 方法来校验两个指标。
  • As new types of data arrive, new tests are needed.
    随着新类型数据的到来，需要新测试。

Know that tests will break—and that's totally normal! You will be able to fix some relatively fast while others may require a significant refactoring because they exposed a hole in the code, and that's OK too! You may also find some errors that are outside your scope, like user entry fields; in these cases it's best to create reports of the erroneous entries and share them with the team responsible to help rectify the problem.

要知道测试会坏——这完全正常！有些你能相对快地修好，另一些可能需要大重构，因为它们暴露了代码里的洞，这也 OK！你还可能发现一些超出你范围的错误，比如用户输入字段；这种情况下最好生成错误条目报告，分享给负责的团队来帮助纠正问题。

While implementing rigorous QA standards does not make you immune from blunders, it does help decrease their frequency and improve overall data sentiment. When folks can focus on the information that the data is telling us, organizations can expect to see higher data literacy and innovation.

虽然实施严格的 QA 标准不能让你免于犯错，但它确实有助于降低错误频率、改善整体数据情绪。当人们能专注于数据告诉我们的信息时，组织可以期待更高的数据素养和创新。

— p.141 —

60. Seven Things Data Engineers Need to Watch Out for in ML Projects数据工程师在 ML 项目中要盯紧的七件事

Dr. Sandeep Uttamchandani

桑迪普·乌塔姆昌达尼 博士

According to a recent estimate, 87% of machine learning (ML) projects fail!¹ This chapter covers the top seven things I have seen go wrong in an ML project from a data-engineering standpoint. The list is sorted in descending order based on the number of times I have encountered the issue multiplied by the impact of the occurrence on the overall project:

根据最近的一项估计，87% 的机器学习（ML）项目都失败了！¹ 本章从数据工程角度讲我见过的 ML 项目最容易出错的七件事。这个列表按“我遇到该问题的次数 × 发生时对整个项目的影响”从高到低排序：

  1. I thought this dataset attribute meant something else. Prior to the big data era, data was curated before being added to the central data warehouse. This is known as schema-on-write. Today, the approach with data lakes is to first aggregate the data and then infer its meaning at the time of consumption. This is known as schema-on-read. As a data engineer, be wary of using datasets without proper documentation of attribute details or a clear data steward responsible for keeping the details updated!
    我以为这个数据集属性是别的意思。大数据时代之前，数据在加入中央数据仓库前会经过整理。这叫写时模式（schema-on-write）。今天数据湖的做法是先聚合数据，在消费时再推断其含义。这叫读时模式（schema-on-read）。作为数据工程师，要警惕使用那些没有恰当属性文档、或没有明确数据负责人维护细节的数据集！
  2. Five definitions exist for the same business metric—which should I use? Derived data or metrics can have multiple sources of truth! For instance, I have seen even basic metrics such as Count of New Customers having multiple definitions across business units. As a data engineer, if a business metric is being used in the model, be sure to look for all the available definitions and their corresponding ETL implementations.
    同一个业务指标有五个定义——我该用哪个？派生数据或指标可能有多个事实源！例如，我见过连“新客户数”这种基础指标，在不同业务部门都有多个定义。作为数据工程师，如果一个业务指标被用在模型里，一定要找齐所有可用定义及其对应的 ETL 实现。
  3. Looks like the data source schema changed. This one is extremely common in large distributed teams. Schema changes at the source database are typically not coordinated with downstream ETL processing teams. Changes can range from schema changes (breaking existing pipelines) to semantic changes that are extremely difficult to debug. Also, when business metrics change, the business definitions lack versioning, making the historic data inconsistent.
    看起来是数据源 schema 变了。这在大型分布式团队里极其常见。源数据库的 schema 变更通常不和下游 ETL 处理团队协调。变更范围可以从 schema 变更（破坏现有管道）到极其难调试的语义变更。而且当业务指标变化时，业务定义缺乏版本管理，让历史数据不一致。
  4. The ETL pipeline logic for training and serving is identical—not really! The typical reason for model performance skew during training and inference is discrepancies in the training and serving pipelines. While the logic may start off identical, fixes made in one pipeline may not be reflected in the other. Especially avoid scenarios in which training and serving pipelines are written in different languages.
    训练和推理的 ETL 管道逻辑是一样的——其实不一样！训练和推理期间模型表现偏差的典型原因，是训练管道和推理管道之间的差异。虽然逻辑一开始可能相同，但在一个管道里做的修复不会反映到另一个。尤其要避免训练和推理管道用不同语言写的情况。
  5. Slow poisoning of the models. It is easier to detect 0–1 kind of errors with data pipelines. The problems that are the most difficult to debug are the ones in which a table is being updated intermittently or is joining to a table that hasn't been updated correctly. In such scenarios, the models will degrade gradually and adjust to the changes. The key is building appropriate circuit breakers to detect and prevent bad-quality data during ingestion.
    模型的缓慢投毒。数据管道更容易检测 0–1 类错误。最难调试的问题是：某张表在间歇性更新、或 join 到一张没被正确更新的表。这种情况下，模型会逐渐退化、适应这些变化。关键是建立合适的熔断器，在数据接入时检测并阻止坏质量数据。
  6. All the datasets managed by a given team have the same quality. This is a classic mistake. Not all datasets from the same team may be reliable. Some might be updated and managed very closely, while others are irregularly updated or have poorly written ETL pipelines! Always develop validation rules for any input data used by the models.
    某个团队管理的所有数据集质量都一样。这是经典错误。同一团队的数据集并不都可靠。有些可能被紧密更新和管理，另一些则不定期更新、或 ETL 管道写得很烂！一定要为模型使用的任何输入数据制定校验规则。
  7. Systematic data issues are causing bias in the overall dataset. If errors in the dataset are random, they are less harmful to model training. But a bug that results in a specific row or column being systematically missing can lead to a bias in the dataset. For instance, if device details of customer clicks are missing for Android users because of a bug, the dataset will be biased for iPhone user activity. Similarly, sudden distribution changes in the data are important to track.
    系统性数据问题正在给整个数据集带来偏差。如果数据集里的错误是随机的，对模型训练危害较小。但一个 bug 导致某行或某列系统性缺失，会给数据集带来偏差。例如，如果因为 bug，Android 用户的客户点击设备细节缺失，数据集就会偏向 iPhone 用户的活动。同样，数据中突然的分布变化也很重要，要追踪。

To wrap up, I believe ML projects are a team sport involving data engineers, data scientists, statisticians, DataOps/MLOps engineers, and business domain experts. Each player needs to play their role in making the project successful.

总结一下，我认为 ML 项目是一项团队运动，涉及数据工程师、数据科学家、统计学家、DataOps/MLOps 工程师和业务领域专家。每个角色都需要发挥作用，让项目成功。

¹ This chapter is a subset of a broader list of "98 Things That Can Go Wrong in an ML Project."

¹ 本章是更广泛的“ML 项目可能出错的 98 件事”列表的一个子集。
